Local Desserts & Sweet Treats in Chattanooga, TN

Original Author: Jack Byrum

This guide covers 15 spots for desserts and sweet treats across Chattanooga. The listings span ice cream shops, bakeries, chocolate shops, cafés, and crêperies.
Clumpies Ice Cream has made small batch ice cream in Chattanooga since 1999 and now runs three locations across the city. The Hot Chocolatier, open since 2008, raised over $19,000 from more than 250 donors in 2024 to survive a forced relocation.
The Southside has the strongest cluster for an afternoon dessert run. Adelle’s Crêperie, Oui Oui Boulangerie, Niedlov’s Bakery, and Scoop Around are all within a few blocks on East Main Street.
The Type filter separates ice cream from bakeries, chocolate shops, and cafés. The Kids filter surfaces the spots with the broadest family appeal, including Rocket Fizz and The Ice Cream Show with its 17,000-combination menu.
If there is a sweet shop worth adding, send an email. Hours and menus change. Confirm before you go.

Ice Cream in Chattanooga.

Clumpies is the local institution, with three locations and a small batch approach going back to 1999. The Ice Cream Show at Walnut Street brings a customizable format with 40 fresh ingredients. Milk & Honey on the North Shore covers the gelato side. Crispy Cones in Ooltewah opened in 2024. The chimney cake format sets it apart from every other shop on this list.

Chattanooga coffee shops

Downtown Chattanooga.

The downtown core holds seven spots in this guide. Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory and The Ice Cream Show are both near Chestnut and Walnut, steps from the Aquarium. Rocket Fizz and Cupcake Kitchen sit on Broad Street. Clumpies has a Market Street location near the Choo Choo. Rembrandt’s Coffee House is a short walk up the bluff in the Arts District.

Downtown museums and exhibits

Southside & East Main.

East Main Street holds four spots in this guide. Oui Oui Boulangerie and Niedlov’s both anchor the morning end of the street. Adelle’s Crêperie handles brunch and evening service. Scoop Around opens at 2pm for the afternoon run. These four are close enough to combine in a single Southside afternoon.

1. The Hot Chocolatier .

A chocolate and confections shop with two Chattanooga locations. The Market Street location is near the Chattanooga Choo Choo. The St. Elmo location sits at the base of Lookout Mountain. Both carry hot chocolate, handmade chocolates, pastries, and gift boxes. The business faced a forced relocation in 2024 and raised over $19,000 from more than 250 community donors. Indoor seating and wifi are available.

2. Rocket Fizz .

A retro candy and soda shop at 411 Broad Street in downtown Chattanooga. Candy bins line the walls for mix and match selections. Shelves hold custom branded sodas, retro favorites, and imported candy from other countries. Open seven days: 10am-9pm Monday through Thursday, 10am-10pm Friday and Saturday, 11am-9pm Sunday.
Google Maps Website
#candy-shop #kids #downtown

3. Belle Chocolates .

A bean to bar chocolatier making handmade chocolates from scratch, starting at the cocoa bean. No fixed retail location. Find them at farmers markets in Chattanooga, Cleveland, and surrounding towns. Available for events and catering. Check their Facebook page for current market schedules and special offerings.
Google Maps Facebook
#chocolate-shop #gifts #farmers-market

4. Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory .

A chocolate and confection shop at 100 Chestnut Street, across from the Tennessee River. The location is steps from the Tennessee Aquarium and next door to Cold Stone Creamery. The shop carries assorted chocolates, caramel apples, truffles, toffee, and clusters. Open daily 11am-10pm.
Google Maps Website
#chocolate-shop #kids #downtown

5. Adelle's Crêperie .

A European style crêperie at 400 East Main Street on the Southside. Sweet crepe options include The Royale with Nutella, strawberries, and chocolate drizzle, and The Bee's Knees with Nutella, bananas, cinnamon maple, and honey. A classic butter and sugar crepe is also available. Open daily 8:30am-2:30pm, with evening service Thursday through Saturday.
Google Maps Website
#cafe #kids #southside

6. Rembrandt's Coffee House .

A European style coffee house at 204 High Street in the Bluff View Arts District. Handmade pastries, craft espresso drinks, and outdoor patio seating. The patio is best in spring and fall. The location is walkable to Hunter Museum, Walnut Street Bridge, and Coolidge Park. Locally made chocolates are available at the counter.
Google Maps Website
#cafe #downtown

7. Milk & Honey .

A gelato counter and brunch café at 135 N Market Street on the North Shore, open since 2013. Gelato and sorbet are made in house with seasonal and year round flavors. The café also serves espresso and from scratch breakfast. Recently renovated into a larger space. Open daily from 6am to 6pm.
Google Maps Website
#ice-cream #cafe #north-shore

8. Oui Oui Boulangerie .

A French bakery at 338 E Main Street on the Southside, inside The Turnbull building. Run by French baker Johann Tremor and his wife Siliza. The case holds pur beurre croissants, pain au chocolat, almond croissants, and berry tarts. Rye bread bakes on Wednesday and Saturday. They sell out early, so go in the morning.
Google Maps Website
#bakery #southside

9. Clumpies Ice Cream .

An ice cream shop open since 1999. Three locations: North Shore, Market Street near the Choo Choo, and St. Elmo near the Incline Railway. Ice cream is made in small batches using self-pasteurized cream and milk. Seasonal flavors rotate throughout the year. Online delivery is available through their website.
Google Maps Website
#ice-cream #kids #north-shore #downtown #st-elmo

10. The Ice Cream Show .

An ice cream shop at 105 Walnut Street at the south end of the Walnut Street Walking Bridge, next to Hunter Museum. Custom flavors blend from over 40 fresh ingredients, with more than 17,000 possible combinations. Dairy-free options include sorbet and oat milk ice cream. Pet-friendly, with a Frosty Paws option for dogs. Open Monday-Thursday noon-9pm, Friday-Saturday noon-11pm, Sunday 2pm-9pm.
Google Maps Website
#ice-cream #kids #downtown

11. Crispy Cones .

A chimney cake ice cream shop at 8898 Old Lee Highway in Ooltewah, opened September 2024. The cone is grilled rotisserie style from pastry dough, rolled in cinnamon sugar, then filled with ice cream and toppings. The concept originated as a Prague street food and reached the area via a Shark Tank investment. Hours run afternoons and evenings. Check the website before visiting.
Google Maps Website
#ice-cream #ooltewah

12. Scoop Around Ice Cream Bar .

A family-run ice cream bar at 831 E Main Street on the Southside. The menu focuses on loaded named creations rather than plain scoops. The Campfire combines chocolate marshmallow ice cream with graham cracker, a Hershey bar, and chocolate drizzle. Four vegan flavors are available. Open daily from 2pm, until 10pm Friday and Saturday.
Google Maps Website
#ice-cream #southside

13. Cupcake Kitchen .

A downtown bakery at 500 Broad Street open seven days a week. Over 20 cupcake flavors bake on-site daily, from classics like vanilla and chocolate to seasonal options like King Cake during Mardi Gras. Gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegan options are available. The shop also carries cookies, cannolis, and cheesecake.
Google Maps
#bakery #kids #downtown

14. Julie Darling Donuts .

A small batch donut shop at 121 Frazier Avenue on the North Shore, open since 2009. Fresh donuts bake each morning and sell out before close. Hours run 7am-1pm Monday through Saturday. Weekend visits may include specialty donuts not on the regular menu. The 1950s retro interior includes a Free Little Library.
Google Maps Website
#bakery #north-shore

15. Niedlov's Bakery & Café .

A bakery and café at 215 E Main Street on the Southside. Sourdough and European style loaves follow a slow bake process from scratch. The pastry case holds croissants, scones, and morning bakes alongside a full café menu. Open 7am-6pm weekdays, 7am-4pm Saturday, closed Sunday.
Google Maps Website
#bakery #cafe #southside
The Southside cluster on East Main is an easy single afternoon run. Oui Oui Boulangerie opens early and sells out fast, so start there. Niedlov’s and Scoop Around are a short walk east on the same street.
On the North Shore, Milk & Honey, Clumpies, and Julie Darling Donuts are all within walking distance of each other. Julie Darling Donuts closes at 1pm, so plan the morning first. For more stops across the city, the Chattanooga coffee guide covers 28 cafés.

FAQ.

Where can I get the best ice cream in Chattanooga?

Clumpies Ice Cream is a local institution with three locations: North Shore, Market Street near the Choo Choo, and St. Elmo. The Ice Cream Show at 105 Walnut Street offers over 17,000 custom combinations from 40 fresh ingredients. Milk & Honey on the North Shore makes house gelato and sorbet. Scoop Around on East Main builds loaded named creations with vegan options available.

What chocolate shops are in Chattanooga?

The Hot Chocolatier has two locations (Market Street and St. Elmo) and carries handmade chocolates, hot drinks, and gift boxes. Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory is at 100 Chestnut Street near the Aquarium. Belle Chocolates sells bean to bar handmade chocolate at farmers markets across the area and does not have a fixed storefront.

Are there vegan or dairy-free dessert options in Chattanooga?

Several spots in this guide carry them. Scoop Around Ice Cream Bar on East Main keeps four vegan flavors. Cupcake Kitchen on Broad Street offers vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free cupcakes. The Ice Cream Show carries sorbet and oat milk ice cream as dairy-free alternatives.

Which Chattanooga dessert shops sell out early?

Julie Darling Donuts at 121 Frazier Avenue on the North Shore bakes a limited batch each morning and closes at 1pm Monday through Saturday. Oui Oui Boulangerie on East Main Street also sells through its baked goods before the end of the day. Both are worth visiting in the morning.

What French bakeries are in Chattanooga?

Oui Oui Boulangerie at 338 E Main Street is Chattanooga’s dedicated French bakery, run by French baker Johann Tremor. The case holds pur beurre croissants, pain au chocolat, almond croissants, and berry tarts. Adelle’s Crêperie at 400 E Main Street serves both sweet and savory French-style crepes.
